problem: RGB semantic segmentation needs high-resolution input, which exposes sensitive content. Existing ways to segment ultra-low-resolution (16x16) RGB (pretrained SR+seg pipelines, mono-module training, naive joint training) perform poorly, and naive joint SR+segmentation training even underperforms freezing the SR module.
motivation: Ultra-low-resolution capture suppresses private information at sensing time and avoids the buffering attack surface of post-capture sanitization. Mobile robots in homes and offices need semantics for downstream tasks such as object-goal navigation. The authors observe that SR quality metrics (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/FID) do not predict segmentation quality at 16x16, and that SR and segmentation objectives conflict in naive joint training.
key_idea: Jointly train an ESRGAN super-resolution branch and a DeepLabv3+ segmentation branch, adding a segmentation-aware discriminator on concatenated (RGB, segmentation) pairs and a foundation-model (AM-RADIO) feature loss, so SR is optimized for semantics rather than pixel fidelity.
insight: At 16x16, RGB reconstruction fidelity is disconnected from segmentation accuracy (PP-Deep has the best PSNR/SSIM but the worst mIoU). Naive joint learning (FJL-Deep, mIoU 0.2575) is worse than freezing SR (MMT-Seg-DF, 0.2855), due to perception-distortion conflict. SAD and AFE each help: removing SAD gives mIoU 0.2824, removing AFE gives 0.3021, versus 0.3101 for the full model. The alpha ablation shows loss balancing matters (best at 0.3). A privacy-vs-mIoU Pareto analysis picks 16x16 as the sweet spot.
method: ESRGAN SR branch: RRDB generator (23 blocks) upsamples the 16x16 RGB to 384x384. It is pretrained with the original ESRGAN losses, then jointly trained.
Segmentation branch: DeepLabv3+ (ResNet-101 + ASPP) on the SR output, trained with pixel-wise cross-entropy. The design accepts any segmentation network.

Agglomerative Feature Extractor (AFE): a frozen AM-RADIO RADIOv2.5-g used only in training. The feature loss is L1 + cosine distance between features of the SR and GT images, replacing VGG perceptual loss.

Segmentation-Aware Discriminator (SAD): discriminates concat(I_gt,S_gt) vs concat(I_sr,S_pred) with BCE (SRGAN-style) and spectral normalization. The generator adversarial loss comes from it, pushing SR outputs toward being useful for segmentation.
Total loss: (1-α)(λ1 L2 + λ2 L_fea + λ3 L_adv) + α L_ce, with λ1=0.5, λ2=0.01, λ3=0.01, α=0.3.

Navigation system: SemanticRecovery (10 ULR images per 360° rotation), FloorBasedNavigation (floor centerline waypoints and branch detection) and ObjectGoalNavigation (approach until the target covers ≥40% of the image).

setting.backbone: ESRGAN generator (RRDB) + DeepLabv3+ (ResNet-101, pretrained), trained jointly; AM-RADIO RADIOv2.5-g as a frozen feature extractor at training only
setting.training_data: SUN RGB-D (10,335 images cropped to 384x384; 9000 train / 668 val / 667 test), 100 epochs, no data augmentation; no other extra data
setting.action_space: navigation: in-place rotations of 10° and forward steps of 20 cm toward floor-centerline waypoints; segmentation itself outputs a 384x384 label map
setting.simulator: real world only (SUN RGB-D for segmentation evaluation)

results: At 16x16 on SUN RGB-D the method reaches mIoU 0.3101 / mAcc 0.4620, beating the best baseline MMT-Seg-DF (0.2855 / 0.3901), and it runs in real time (~17.6 FPS). In real-robot object-goal navigation it reaches 85.0% success versus 65.0% (MMT-Seg-DF) and 62.5% (FJL-Deep), against 92.5% for the full-resolution upper bound. The privacy non-leakage rate is 1.0 at 16x16 (readability-aware prompt).
limitations: Boundary segmentation is weak (low BF score, color bleeding at edges).
ULR inputs are simulated by downsampling rather than captured by native ULR sensors.
Privacy is evaluated with a VLM-based proxy on a small dataset (130 images), not a formal guarantee; the real-world segmentation and navigation tests are small (90 images, 40 trials).
